the ion transfer potential at liquid-liquid boundaries can be decomposed into a static and a dynamic component, that the static component is determined by the partition coefficients and is localized at the interface, and that the dynamic component is governed by the mean partition coefficient of the salt and the diffusion coefficients and expands with time.

the ion transfer potentials across a liquid junction between two electrolyte solutions are the sum of a static component that depends only on the single ion partition coefficients, and a dynamic component that depends only upon the mean partition coefficient and the ion diffusion coefficients.

the ion transfer potential at liquid-liquid junctions can be decomposed into two separable components, a localized static component that depends solely on the single ion partition coefficients of the ions and a dynamic component that depends on the partition coefficients of the salt as well as the diffusion coefficients of all the ions.
